title: TERMINATOR 2 / MIDWAY MOUNTED-GUN UPRIGHT
variant: Midway blue Arnold/T2 sides, white title, red molding and two fixed-base machine guns
preview_note: 32 x 48 px | Midway blue Arnold/T2 sides, white title, red molding and two fixed-base machine guns

rom_validation.matching: All required files match pinned FBNeo CRC32 and size; existing legacy aliases are accepted.

cabinet.purpose: Photographed Midway Terminator 2 cabinet: blue Arnold/T2 side print, white Midway/title marks, red molding, black front, fixed gun bases and machine-gun handles rather than ordinary joysticks.
cabinet.rights: Underlying printed artwork Midway / Carolco / licensors; third-party archive, not publisher authorization. Photo/scan author, replacement-print status and redistribution permission remain unverified.

marquee.purpose: White Terminator 2 Judgment Day title and blue Arnold portrait rectified from the same cabinet photo; no console/movie box art is substituted.
marquee.rights: Underlying printed artwork Midway / Carolco / licensors; third-party archive, not publisher authorization. Photo/scan author, replacement-print status and redistribution permission remain unverified.

controls.purpose: Archive control photo indexed term2la3; the cabinet artwork is common to the game revisions, while the supplied ROM remains LA4. Cyberdyne blue/red Arnold operator deck, blue/red Start buttons, gun-base/trigger/grenade details and lower instructions. Printed center/caption patches are extracted without baking photographed 3D guns into the flat deck.
controls.rights: Underlying printed artwork Midway / Carolco / licensors; third-party archive, not publisher authorization. Photo/scan author, replacement-print status and redistribution permission remain unverified.

flyer.purpose: 1991 Midway promotional print describing two-player gun operation and carrying Midway/Carolco/licensor credits; corroborates game/cabinet identity, not copyright permission.
flyer.rights: Underlying printed artwork Midway / Carolco / licensors; third-party archive, not publisher authorization. Photo/scan author, replacement-print status and redistribution permission remain unverified.

screen.purpose: Real 400x255 game display from supplied LA4 ROMs and existing Midway WASM core: nine-coin startup, Start 15 frames, one first-action confirmation, then 2000 neutral frames. TMS34010 emits one fewer scanline than initial 400x256 geometry; actual output dimensions are retained.
screen.rights: Game imagery Midway / Carolco / licensors, captured from user-supplied local ROM only. No ROM downloaded, uploaded or committed; no redistribution license inferred.

uncertainties: Publisher-hosted artwork masters were not found. Archive photographs/scans are not proof of factory prints or artwork redistribution permission.
This selected shell/kit interpretation is explicit; ROM, hardware and seat count are not changed to suit artwork. No map placement or uploads included.
One photographed side is reused on the opposite side with readable lettering; the distinct opposite factory print is unverified and is not invented.

Two mounted machine guns with gray receiver, barrel, grip and fixed base are modeled separately; no ball-top joystick is substituted. Two small red action details per gun represent trigger/grenade controls, not panel firing buttons; Start buttons remain photographed.
The panel photo is indexed under LA3 but supplies common physical cabinet art, not the ROM/software. The supplied game/driver remains LA4, with all 17 required files matching CRC/size.

Terminator 2's relative gun axes accept the existing RetroPad directions through FBNeo's fake-digital fallback. Both guns and saved aiming positions have been checked with independent-seat movement and RAM replay, alongside ordinary two-player/spectator checks. Pointer/mouse aiming is not implemented.
Some TMS34010 outputs crop the last advertised scanline. Capture validation accepts only that one-row crop or the corresponding rotation, while still requiring valid machine RAM and image geometry.
input_note: Arrow keys / touch D-pad move the gun using FBNeo fake-digital relative axes; the existing action keys fire and throw grenades. Independent guns keep their positions in core savestates. Mouse aiming is not added or claimed.
